description: This is a team from the Department of Computer Science and Information Engineering at Taipei City University of Science and Technology, aiming to leverage computer science and sports science to benefit astronauts and technologies related to space satellites.
summary:
Smart Sports Spaces & Crowd Analytics (Focus on Urban Infrastructure & Data)
We developed a Smart Urban Sports & Health Analytics Platform that integrates spatial data algorithms from computer science with physiological load models from sports science, synthesizing real-time crowd flow and environmental sensor data across city parks and sports centers. To address unequal access to urban fitness spaces and the lack of scientific exercise guidance, our system dynamically recommends optimal workout times and personalized exercise prescriptions for citizens while helping municipalities optimize facility planning. This matters because it enhances public workout safety and efficiency, reduces chronic disease healthcare burdens, and builds a healthier, more sustainable, and resilient city.
details:
This project introduces a Smart Urban Sports & Health Analytics Platform that bridges Spatial Data Science and Exercise Physiology, delivering dual-sided value for both citizens and municipal planners:

  • Citizen Portal (Personalized Smart Exercise Routing):
    • Real-Time Venue Recommendation & Crowd Forecasting: Integrates live crowd density and micro-climate sensor data—including Air Quality Index (AQI), Wet-Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT), and UV levels—across city parks, riverside trails, and public sports centers to dynamically recommend the nearest, least crowded, and safest workout venues and time slots.
    • Science-Backed Personalized Exercise Prescriptions: Automatically generates and adjusts training intensities (heart rate zones, pacing, and Metabolic Equivalents [METs]) alongside hydration reminders based on the user's fitness baseline, fatigue recovery status, and real-time environmental heat load.
    • Resource Allocation & Equity Diagnostics: Uses spatial hotspot and isochrone accessibility analysis to visualize "fitness service deserts" across districts, enabling local governments to prioritize new facility investments, night-lighting upgrades, and public bike-share rebalancing.
